summary: FinSight Labs: sudden tail-latency & 5xx increase after mixed-quant + aggressive batching; request diagnostic + safe switchover plan
description: Issue summary: After applying a tenant-scoped optimizer profile combining mixed quantization (q4_0 for majority layers, int8 for attention) with aggressive batching (max_batch_size=1024, batch_timeout_ms=12) and enabling prefix KV prefetch, FinSight Labs began seeing 95th/99th percentile token latencies spike and a small but growing number of 5xx errors for chat streaming endpoints. Impact: customer-facing chat feature shows degraded latency and occasional aborted streams; revenue-impacting for peak trading-hours traffic. Environment: dedicated pool (fin-tenant-pool-3), prod, us-east-1. Model: gpt-open-16k-q4_0-mixed pinned at v2026-03-09-21:00.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Apply tenant optimizer profile 'fin-mixed-2026-03-09' via Console > Optimizer Profiles for FinSight tenant.
2) Send sustained chat traffic (avg concurrency ~150 requests, peak bursts to 400) with streaming responses enabled.
3) Observe latencies and 5xx rate over 10-20 minutes.
4) Revert profile to baseline (gpt-open-16k-base) and observe improvements in ~2-5 minutes.
observed_behavior:
- 95p token latency increased from ~120ms to ~460ms.
- 99p spikes to 900ms+ intermittently.
- 5xx rate rose from 0.02% to 0.8% during peak bursts.
- GPU utilization on pool nodes dropped to 35-50% while CPU and PCIe stalls increased.
- Streaming sessions show frequent 'stream aborted' logs originating from serving runtime's kv-prefetch module.
expected_behavior: After optimizer change, we expect similar or improved token latency and stable 5xx rates; GPU utilization should remain high for throughput-focused batches and stalls should not increase significantly.
logs:
Attached logs (referenced in Slack thread):
- /var/log/fin-tenant-pool-3/serving-runtime/2026-03-09-21:15-22:30.log
- stacktrace excerpts: "serving.runtime.kv_prefetch: timeout waiting for prefetch (200ms)"
- Nginx upstream 502 traces around 2026-03-10T15:42:10Z
- P95/P99 latency series from dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/fin-sight/latency?from=2026-03-09T20:00&to=2026-03-10T16:00
initial_analysis: Support observed mismatch between batching expectations and quantized execution path. Hypotheses: (1) Mixed-quant kernel selection causes slower per-token execution for certain sequence-length distributions resulting in increased tail latency during bursts; (2) KV prefetch adds contention leading to timeouts and aborted streams; (3) Aggressive batching parameter combined with low GPU occupancy triggers inefficient kernel paths and PCIe thrashing. Early metrics: increased PCIe transfer time and higher memcpy stalls were visible in node perf counters. No model corruption detected.
investigation_notes:
- Replayed a sample of FinSight prod traffic against non-quantized baseline: tail latency returned to expected range.
- Replayed same traffic against mixed-quant profile in staging with identical hardware: reproduced 95p latency rise but only under bursty concurrency patterns.
- Microbenchmarks show attention kernels in int8 fallback paths have higher variance for sequence lengths > 1024.
- KV prefetch queue length increased under aggressive batch windows; prefetch timeouts align with aborted stream timestamps.
- Related GH PR for runtime prefetch guards: #1459 (linked above) may reduce timeouts but needs careful validation.

2026-03-11 11:12 - Customer (FinSight SRE - Elliot Chen): Prefers a conservative approach; requests a plan that guarantees no dropped requests and minimal latency degradation while rolling back. Asks for specific traffic split and timing guidance.

proposed_workaround:
1) Snapshot current optimizer profile 'fin-mixed-2026-03-09' (console snapshot + backup; keep immutable copy).
2) Apply per-tenant override: set max_batch_size=256, batch_timeout_ms=6, disable kv_prefetch=false->true (toggle off prefetch).
3) Canary at 5% traffic for 10 minutes, then 25% for 15 minutes, monitor 95/99p and 5xx.
4) If stable, progressively promote to 100% over controlled windows.
Note: If latencies remain high after per-tenant batching reduction, plan to pin to gpt-open-16k-base model variant and route traffic to baseline for up to 30 minutes while teams validate fixes.
resolution_notes: In progress: Step 1 snapshot completed. Canary of reduced batching (5%) shows improvement. Full rollback to baseline model variant (non-quantized) is scheduled as contingency and will be executed if canary metrics do not sustain improvement by 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC. Engineering to merge prefetch guard PR #1459 for longer-term fix and validate on staging before tenant re-enable.
follow_up_actions:
- Engineering to run extended stage validation of PR #1459 and provide ETA for safe re-enable of kv-prefetch per-tenant.
- Product/Support to coordinate a postmortem with FinSight SRE describing root cause and recommended optimizer profile guidelines for bursty workloads.
- Add a console check that warns when mixed-quant + high max_batch_size is enabled for tenants with bursty concurrency patterns.
- Document a rollback script (ops/runbooks/fin-sight-optimizer-rollback.sh) and link to ticket.
notes_for_customer: We understand impact during critical trading hours — our immediate goal is a safe, staged rollback that avoids interrupting active requests. Current approach: snapshot profile, sequentially reduce batching and disable prefetch in a canary fashion. We will keep FinSight SRE updated on each canary step and schedule baseline pin if needed. Expected timeline for initial mitigation results: within 30 minutes of the canary start. Engineering will provide a permanent fix timeline after staging validation of the prefetch guard PR.
